speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Transport in view of the rise in fires caused by active mobility devices (AMDs) in 2023 (a) what are the Ministry’s plans to carry out enforcement against the retailers and distributors of non-original AMD batteries; and (b) whether the Ministry intends to increase the penalties for individuals who are found to have tampered with or modified their AMD batteries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It is an offence to illegally modify, sell or use such devices on public paths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) conducts enforcement on paths and operations against retailers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Non-compliant devices are immediately seized and enforcement actions are taken.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We will press on with our enforcement and public education efforts, and will review the need for further measures.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Beyond enforcement, is the Ministry considering collaborating with retailers and distributors to educate consumers on identifying safe and certified active mobility device (AMD) batteries?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, given the rise in some of these fires involving AMDs, is the Ministry considering stricter safety regulations for all AMDs, including mandatory fire retardant casings or automatic shut-off mechanisms for some of these machines?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Yes, LTA already engages PAB retailers for them to collaborate with the National Delivery Champions Association to conduct workshops on the safe use of some of the more popular PAB brands used by delivery riders.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: On a more general basis, the LTA and Singapore Civil Defence Force co-chair an Active Mobility Fire Safety Taskforce that coordinates efforts to raise awareness among the public of fire safety and proper use of devices, whether through face-to-face interactions or through social media.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: On additional requirements for fire retardant features of the devices, if the devices are compliant with the standards – we have separate standards for PMDs and PABs – these batteries should work if they are used properly and charged in a proper manner.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The authorities will continue to review these standards and also consider the suggestion by the Member on whether additional device features are needed for better fire safety.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary highlighted the harsh punishments when retailers are caught with selling illegal batteries or devices.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share with the House, despite these harsh punishments, what are the challenges that LTA face in trying to clamp down on the number of retailers selling illegal devices as well as illegal batteries?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For some of these devices, they may be purported to be very good and very reasonably priced, but they may be constructed for use in a different climate, in different terrain, than Singapore's.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, I would urge consumers to keep their eyes and ears open, and look out for the right devices to purchase.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have got two questions to follow up with the Ministry of Transport.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would the Ministry consider, looking at ways to conduct enforcement operations against online platforms with a presence in Singapore, with an office in Singapore, that may have facilitated the sale of a non-compliant battery that is a fire risk?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: There is no law per se, but we are currently reviewing how we can strengthen this aspect of regulation.
